name: Eggs baked in ajvar with feta and torn sourdough
intro: The month's jar, loosened with a little water, becomes a skillet of smoky pepper sauce. Four eggs set in it, feta goes over the top, and sourdough does the rest.
needs: Olive oil, chile flakes, and salt

steps.text: Warm 1 tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium. Add the garlic and a pinch of chile flakes and stir until it smells good — don't let it brown.
Add the ajvar and ½ cup water, stir, and simmer until it's loose and bubbling, like a thick tomato sauce.
Make four wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon, crack an egg into each, and salt the eggs.
Cover the pan and cook over medium-low until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble. Check at 5 minutes; they go from runny to hard quickly.
Meanwhile, toast the sourdough in a dry pan or under the broiler, and drizzle it with olive oil.
Feta and arugula over the pan, a little olive oil, and the toast torn alongside for dragging through the sauce.

how_it_works: This is shakshuka's method with a different sauce: any thick, flavorful sauce can poach eggs if you loosen it to the texture of a tomato sauce and cover the pan, so the tops cook in steam while the bottoms stay soft. The salty feta and the bread are there because the sauce is sweet and smoky and wants something to cut it and something to carry it.
swaps: Crumble in leftover lamb or sausage before the eggs go in.
A spoonful of salted yogurt instead of feta.
No bread? Spoon it over rice.
leftovers: Eggs don't reheat well, but extra sauce keeps for days. Make more and poach fresh eggs in it tomorrow.
